blurb: Wetlands, groundwater-dependent ecosystems, rivers and streams, floodplains and freshwater species richness (report Table 13).

method: Wetlands are the National Wetlands Inventory's freshwater emergent, freshwater forested/shrub, and estuarine and marine wetland types in California; groundwater-dependent ecosystems are the GDE vegetation and wetland layers (Klausmeyer et al. 2018). Both are measured on whole resolution-10 cells (about 3.7 acres), which overstates the extent of small wetlands but not their conserved share. The 100-year floodplain row uses FEMA's flood hazard map (Special Flood Hazard Areas); the report used First Street Foundation flood zones, which this catalog does not carry, so the two are different features. Freshwater species richness marks HUC12 watersheds in California's top 20% (Howard et al. 2015). Streams use the NHDPlus High Resolution network, with stream order from that network, restricted to California's land grid and measured by length: each flowline's length is spread over the cells it crosses. That network carries roughly three times the channel length of the medium-resolution network behind the report, so shares compare and lengths do not. Wetlands and groundwater-dependent ecosystems are Key Features in the report; the freshwater-richness row is a value-based feature with no need class.
